verdict.rationale: Honeycomb's own Triggers and SLOs are rules you configure once that keep watching for threshold breaches and fire alerts or custom webhooks when conditions are met. That is a background automation, but it is limited to alerting. The API and MCP server are only building blocks or user-driven agent access, so they get no credit. Missing for 10: autonomous agentic background workflows (e.g., agents that investigate or remediate unattended), scheduled or recurring automation beyond alert evaluation, and any independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Use triggers to send alerts when thresholds that you define and configure are passed.
Set up Triggers and SLOs to alert your team when conditions are met, and route notifications to Slack, PagerDuty, Microsoft Teams, or a custom webhook.
This allows you to build custom integrations that receive JSON payloads from Honeycomb upon alerts firing.
Route Honeycomb Trigger and SLO burn alerts to any service that accepts a JSON payload, including third-party tools and custom integrations.
